label: GPT-6.1 Sol
output:
To: timeline
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: none

Spent the last two Saturdays redoing the electric in a buddy’s shed. Figured it was going to be a little cleanup job.

It was not a little cleanup job.

The power supply was THREE orange extension cords plugged into each other, coming out a basement window, across the yard and under the deck. Apparently the plan was to keep adding cord until electricity found the shed.

Opened things up and found a splice wrapped in duct tape. Not electrical tape. Duct tape. Somewhere there’s a roll of electrical tape sitting on a shelf wondering what it did wrong.

Had a 30 amp breaker feeding 14 gauge wire. For the folks who don’t do this for a living, that breaker is supposed to protect the wire. You don’t put a bigger breaker on undersized wire and call it an upgrade. That’s like fixing the smoke alarm by taking the battery out.

One outlet was wired with speaker wire. I checked. It was not playing music.

Then I found the “GFCI.”

Regular outlet. GFCI sticker.

That was the whole system. A sticker. By that logic I’m putting a Corvette sticker on my truck tomorrow and seeing what happens on 51.

Ceiling fan box was hanging on by ONE drywall screw. That screw had more responsibility than most foremen I’ve worked for.

Mouse nest in a junction box, too. Mice were fine. Completely unbothered. Only occupants on the property who apparently approved the electrical inspection.

But my favorite was inside the panel door, written in Sharpie:

SHED - DONT TOUCH - RON

Buddy’s wife is standing there when I open it and says, “Who’s Ron?”

Like I’d know. Lady, I just got here. All I know about Ron is he doesn’t want anybody checking his work.

Now before everybody starts piling on, I don’t think whoever did this was evil. Cheap and a little proud, probably. Most of these jobs aren’t somebody trying to hurt anyone. It’s somebody figuring “that’ll work” enough times in a row that eventually you’ve got speaker wire in a wall and a sticker doing the job of a safety device.

And that’s the serious part. This stuff burns houses down. An outlet working does NOT mean it’s safe. A fan spinning does not mean it’s going to stay on the ceiling. “Never had a problem” isn’t much comfort when the first problem is a fire.

We got the questionable stuff out, put in a proper buried feed, actual GFCI protection, proper boxes and outlets, and a brace for the fan. No more extension-cord obstacle course.

Paid in two pizzas and a case of Yuengling. Pizza came after the work. I do have standards.

Please, hire a licensed electrician. Not your buddy whose qualifications are a screwdriver and three YouTube videos.

And if the safety equipment turns out to be a sticker, stop using it and make the call.
